export_note: Selected fields from the completed native grade; machine-local paths are omitted. The mathematical grade is preserved.

grade.first_issue: The decisive claim that the remaining expression simplifies to \(PB=PC\) is asserted without calculation, while the cross-angle conditions \(\angle LBK=\beta\) and \(\angle LCK=\gamma\) are never translated into usable relations.
grade.summary: The proof correctly reduces \(OM=ON\) to \(PB=PC\) for \(P=2O\) and derives some valid preliminary trigonometric relations. However, it omits the entire central compatibility argument and also contains sign errors in expanding \(P\cdot(\vec b-\vec c)\). Thus the conclusion is not established.
strengths: Correctly reduces the desired midpoint-distance equality to showing that \(P=2O\) lies on the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\).
Correctly obtains \(PK\perp AK\), \(PL\perp AL\), and useful sine-law formulas for \(AK\) and \(AL\).

errors.description: The statement that the terms “balance” and force \(PB=PC\) is an unsupported decisive inference replacing the central proof.
The conditions \(\angle LBK=\beta\) and \(\angle LCK=\gamma\) are not actually used to derive equations constraining \(A,\theta_K,\phi_L\).
The expansion of \(P\cdot(\vec b-\vec c)\) reverses the signs of the terms involving \(c\); the displayed trigonometric expression therefore does not follow from the preceding line.
